title: Quarterly roadmap: Architecting the Hosted API & Model Catalog runway
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Produce a prioritized, executable quarterly roadmap that ties hosted API product work to model-catalog lifecycle controls, rollout gating, and runway capacity assumptions. This ticket captures the PM-level orchestration: scope decisions, acceptance gates, rollout cadence, and cross-functional dependencies required to ship a cohesive host+catalog quarter. The outcome will be a published roadmap artifact, stakeholder signoff, and a set of aligned tickets for each tranche (canary, pilot, GA).
background: We continue to onboard model variants into the hosted catalog while customers expect predictable latency and stable SLAs. Recent capacity variability and a handful of model regressions exposed gaps in our release gating and runway assumptions. This initiative aims to reduce release risk by formalizing per-model acceptance criteria, standardized canary windows, and a runway plan that ties model rollout velocity to Dedicated capacity and autoscale policies.
plan: 1) Inventory: consolidate all candidate models and hosted endpoints slated for the quarter, including owners, expected traffic, and QA signals. 2) Define gates: propose a mandatory gate checklist (performance profile, regression evals, canary traffic ranges, rollback plan). 3) Phasing: group models into tranches that map to capacity and risk (low-risk fast, medium-risk staged, high-risk pilot-only). 4) Sync: run cross-functional review sessions (Eng, RD, Console, SRE, Security) to validate assumptions. 5) Publish: create final roadmap artifact and convert tranches into execution tickets with owners and timelines.
acceptance_criteria: Consolidated model catalog spreadsheet with owner, expected Q usage, and performance profile
Gate checklist defined and added to PRD and release playbook
Tranche assignments for all models with estimated capacity impact
Cross-functional signoff recorded in the roadmap doc and a stakeholder list
Execution tickets created for each tranche with clear owners and due dates
milestones: 2025-02-12: Inventory complete and initial risk tagging
2025-02-18: Draft gate checklist shared with Eng & SRE
2025-02-22: Tranche grouping and capacity estimates validated
2025-03-03: Roadmap artifact published and execution tickets created
risks: Capacity estimates are optimistic and may require additional Dedicated commits
Regression evals might reveal quality issues that delay planned tranches
Stakeholder alignment friction could push signoff past intended dates
Telemetry gaps could make it hard to set reliable canary thresholds
updates: 2025-02-12: Inventory phase completed ahead of schedule; initial list is 28 models with two high-risk candidates.
2025-02-14: Eng flagged a kernel scheduling dependency (ENG-2990) that may shift medium-risk tranche later by 1 sprint.
2025-02-15: Security requested a short review for models that access customer-provided prompts; added to gate checklist.
